paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled 'QAdapter,' illustrates the number of FLOPs (floating point operations) required by different fine-tuning methods. The horizontal axis contains the category labels for each method, listed from left to right as: Full FT, TAG, Adapter, MTL-FT, QAdapter, and Ours. The vertical axis is labeled '# FLOPs' and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 10^18 to 10^20. The first five bars are colored orange, while the final bar labeled 'Ours' is colored dark green and appears in bold text on the category axis, visually distinguishing it from the other methods. The tallest bar is Full FT, with an approximate value near 6×10^19. TAG and Adapter have similar heights, both approximately 2×10^19. MTL-FT is shorter at roughly 4×10^18. QAdapter and Ours are the shortest bars, both near 1.5×10^18 to 2×10^18, with very similar heights. The bars appear to be arranged in a roughly descending order of FLOPs from left to right, with the exception that Ours is slightly taller than QAdapter. The chart is not grouped or stacked, and there is no legend present.
